utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Delivering the food to the population of the Srebrenica enclave in this manner, did it improve the situation in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: No, it could not have improved the situation because this type of aid was available only to those who were physically and able and healthy. I couldn't get that food because as a wounded man I couldn't go and fight with other residents to get some food. I know that the elderly, the women and children, could not get their hands on any of that food, nobody would bring the food to you and tell you, "Well, here, this belongs to you."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with any attacks launched from the Srebrenica enclave on the nearby Serbian villages, specifically Kravica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you continue there, we have heard, if not ten times, then at least seven to eight times, about these attacks. Is there any dispute that there were attacks launched around Srebrenica from within Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There is no dispute. It was actually part of the opening statement, although I think -- I don't know where Mr. Stojanovic is going with this, but it may be relevant to examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither do I. So I do not know whether Mr. Stojanovic wants to ask the witness whether he has knowledge of it which seems to be pretty irrelevant, unless there are specific reasons to ask these questions. And Mr. Stojanovic, is it just to establish something that is not in dispute? That's a waste of time. Could you please think about where you're heading for and then continue without any risk of wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This was just an introduction to my following question, which stems from the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During the examination-in-chief, you mentioned the reasons for the hatred due to which you were afraid of remaining in the territory of Srebrenica. These reasons for the mutual hatred that existed there, is it in any way linked to these events that I just asked you about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: No, it's not linked in any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Pause between question and answer and between answer and question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, my mistake. I am not linking this in any way whatsoever. If you wish, I can talk at length about the ways and manner of resistance put up by people of Srebrenica. I was simply familiar with the situation because I witnessed it on a daily basis, but I'm not connecting this with hatred. There was hatred in Srebrenica already at the beginning of the war. If hadn't been any hatred displayed, why was Srebrenica put under a blockade? Why didn't they leave a corridor, and why didn't everyone sit down and agree and say, "Gentlemen, we need to reach an agreement, we need to evacuate the population," so all this intense hatred among the Serb population and the army started from the very beginning and it only deepened with time in the way that you mentioned, and that is when people had to go to the Serbian villages looking for food. Imagine us being kept in this courtroom for five or six months without any food. What can we do? We have to break through a door and try to find food somewhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you've answered the question. Next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, Mr. Mladic is trying to get your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, I can hear you speaking, so therefore the volume is too high. Mr. Stojanovic, the Chamber is really concerned about hearing repetitious evidence which we have heard a lot of times, whereas this witness primarily, I think, was called to testify about the executions which he escaped, and all the rest until now is for the seventh up to the tenth time that we hear such evidence. We don't need it a hundred times, especially when it's not in dispute. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me this? On the 11th of July, 1992 [as interpreted], did you and your family receive any instruction from anyone on where to go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't receive any instructions relating to me personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are recorded as having said 1992. Is that the year you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. I said 11th July 1995. It may have been the slip of the tongue but I think I said 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's how the witness understood it as well, Witness RM249? I see you're nodding yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I understood that the gentleman was asking me about 1995, and I gave the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'm looking at the clock. It's time for a break. A break now of 20 minutes, Witness, and not much longer. We first move into closed session before we take that break, and we will resume in closed session after the break in order to allow the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Stojanovic, you don't have to make a pause before you start, but immediately after the first answer, you have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We can continue, Witness? Before you decided to head off towards Potocari, a large group of men passed by you in the opposite direction. Did you know where they were heading to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes. In my statement I said that these people were moving towards Potocari. My house is located in the place whose name I mentioned in my statement. So from that position, it was possible to observe the column of people passing by. It is possible that I mentioned a group leaving towards Potocari. It was clear to me that the people of Srebrenica were leaving Srebrenica seeking salvation in the area of Potocari with the Dutch Battalion. Being wounded, I also understood that the only way for me to seek shelter would be to go to the DutchBat. Therefore, I didn't have any dilemma as to which direction to take. That is to say, I decided to go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please focus your answers very much on what is asked? The only question was whether you knew where they were heading to, not whether you had any hesitation where to go for yourself or whatever. Mr. Stojanovic, next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see, before you started towards Potocari, any armed men moving towards Jaglici and Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Not in that area. I wasn't able to see that. If you are familiar with this region, this area is far away from the place that you have just mentioned. Perhaps one kilometre or maybe even more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said no, I had no opportunity to see it in that area. That fully answers the question. If Mr. Stojanovic wants to know the reasons why, he'll ask you for it. Next question, please, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Upon your arrival in Potocari, you were given information that General Mladic had come there. What was exactly said to you about what General Mladic told the refugees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: The people in Potocari who told me that General Mladic had arrived passed this information from mouth to mouth, and that is how I learned about his arrival. I wasn't able to understand any orders that he had given. I only learned from people close to me that the general had arrived in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any information that General Mladic addressed the refugees and guaranteed safety to all of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I couldn't comprehend that in the sense that you are stating it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please have P1990 under seal. We need page 2 in both versions. The penultimate paragraph. And then I'll move on to the last paragraph. So once again I please would like to remind that this not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let us look together at this, and please focus on the third paragraph from the bottom in both the English and the B/C/S versions, where, in the statement that you gave at the time, and by which you stood fully, as you said today, you said that you heard from some women that General Mladic was in Potocari and that he delivered a speech guaranteeing security to all the refugees. Do you stand by this assertion in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Your question was addressed to me, whether I felt any security and safety guaranteed by Mr. Mladic, and I told you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that is at least not how we understood the question. I think the question, as Mr. Stojanovic put it to you now, was the one he wanted to put and that question has been answered. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So we can confirm that you fully stand by this portion of your statement, "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I fully stand by this statement. However, your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. I'm going to proceed. Please look at the last paragraph in your statement, where there is mention of a name. I'm going to read it. Where you say I saw Ibran Mustafovic. Now, my question is: Is this a proper spelling of the last name of this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes. I also noticed a mistake here. It should read "Mustafic" instead of "Mustafovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you have before you, you say admitting that this was a 1996 statement, that this man was taken away during that day and you have never seen him again. Do you know today whether this person is still alive or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes. Not only that I have this information, but it is common knowledge that this gentleman, who tried in many ways to ingratiate himself and become politically active, I think that he was condemned by the entire public of Srebrenica for everything that he did, and that he still may be doing to this day by the way he is treating the people of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question, sorry, if I may just interrupt, Mr. Stojanovic, I don't think the witness answered the question you asked. Do you know whether this man is still alive or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He is alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that during his stay in Srebrenica, before July 1995, he was the subject of an attempted assassination and that he was wounded in the process?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Believe me, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court what was Mr. Mustafic doing on the day when you saw him on that particular date when you were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I have to give you a rather lengthy answer. Mr. Mustafic had been politically active before the war. He was known to a lot of people and that's why I recognised had him as well. He was accompanied by a gentleman I think called Hamed who was also a political activist. I found it strange that these two men were together in the same area because they were politically active before the war. After that, I saw some Serb soldiers in the company of Mustafic and they all left together. I said that Mustafic is still alive, and how he managed to survive, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is the little pause. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when you saw him, was the procedure of boarding the buses by the refugees already in progress?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I believe that was on the first day following our arrival. I don't know if they tried to carry out the evacuation on that first day. I know it started on the second day. So towards the evening of the first day, that is to say in the afternoon on the 11th of July, proper evacuation would actually start on the 12th of July. Now, I can tell you that I'm not sure whether there was any evacuation carried out on the evening of the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have your statement in front of you and you said that you saw this gentleman on the 12th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes. That was the second time. I first saw him, as I described a minute ago, as soon as I arrived in Potocari, I spotted him, and the last time he was seen on the 12th together with the Serbian soldiers who took him away. Yes, the evacuation was on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have now 1D1046 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, while we're waiting for the document to be uploaded, let me ask you this: Do you know that the gentleman we are discussing now published a book about the events he experienced, and have you read that book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: What I read is the daily press. I read it on internet. And in the daily press, I read that this gentleman published a book. I know nothing more about the book, not a single page of its content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the simple question -- the simple answer to the question whether you read the book is no, you didn't read it. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we need to correct the number. 1D00084. This is the 65 ter number. 1D00084. Could we see page 387 of the book, of this exhibit? And I would like to see the last paragraph underlined.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He says in the book, which is called "Planned Chaos," in describing the same days in July 1995, he says: "During that time, on the little bridge across the Rabin creek and manned by Chetniks, several soldiers of the Dutch Battalion, Nesib Mandic, Ibro Nuhanovic, and Camila were together letting through and separating the people. Do you know, sir, who Nesib Mandic is, Ibro and Nuhanovic and who Camila is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Personally I didn't know Nesib Mandic. I didn't know personally Ibro Nuhanovic, nor Madam Camila. However, by reading the papers, I know that they were the people who tried to conduct some sort of negotiations during the time when the people were in Potocari. This is what I know from the papers, from the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He goes on to say: "I knew they had been in Bratunac negotiating but I could not believe my eyes that, that several Dutch soldiers were working together with the Chetniks and separating people." My question is: Did you have an opportunity to see what Ibran Mustafic describes in his book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The next topic I want to ask you is this: When you went off to board buses, is it true that members of international forces put up two APCs in a funnel shape, together with red ribbons thus directing the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. But it wasn't in the funnel shape. It was on each side of the road and between those two APCs, there was a passage for those who wished to go towards the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the narrowest point of that passage between the two APCs, there were members of international forces who let through towards the buses some of the people proportionate to the number who could board the buses. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes. Let me explain. The first point of contact were the soldiers of the Dutch Battalion. Once they let people through, then the people would get to the Serb soldiers who checked them again, and the Serb soldiers, when conducting their checks, would separate the people, men from women and children. Women and children were given an option to go towards the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far was the place where the Serb soldiers separated the men from the rest of the group? How far was that place from the place where the members of international forces were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: That was immediately behind the two APCs used by the Dutch soldiers. I can't tell you the exact distance in metres, but ten or so, ten metres from the place where the Dutch soldiers stood to the place where the Serbian soldiers stood, perhaps even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On that morning, when you set out to board the buses which, according to your statement, was on the 13th of July at about 8.00 in the morning, were there any buses there at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I need to answer in a couple of sentences, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: As I passed through, a group of Serbian soldiers distanced themselves in a very short time, perhaps less than a minute, and for me that was enough time to allow me to enter the last bus which was some ten metres to the front, perhaps even less than ten metres. So that's all I needed to get on the bus. Once I got on the bus, I heard the voice of the Serb soldiers asking, "Did any of the men enter buses?" And everybody kept quiet. I was afraid that one of the women would tell me, "Why don't you go and report yourself?" But none of them did. Following that, another group of women and children boarded and they completely concealed me. I sat on the floor of the bus and women and children who boarded right behind me hid me, so I was completely concealed on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like for us to look at the transcript of the testimony of a witness in this trial, a member of the DutchBat, describing precisely the same event at the same time, morning hours of 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we see, Your Honours, in e-court, the testimony dated 25th of April 2013, page of transcript, 10381, lines 10 to 20, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In this case, I take it? This case, yes. Now, do you want to put to the witness is there any inconsistency or is it consistent?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it's inconsistent and that's precisely why I want to put this portion to the witness. It was in this trial, as I have stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, now, have you -- if you want to show this to the witness, have you uploaded that portion of the testimony in e-court? Because otherwise, it might be difficult for --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I did. I asked for specific lines and I would read them out in B/C/S so that we can follow. So it's page 10381, lines 10 to 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, by way of introduction, let me tell you again that this is the testimony of a member of the DutchBat speaking about the 13th of July morning hours. The question of the Prosecutor was: "Q. Sir, on the second morning of the evacuation, that time period when the Serbs had not yet arrived, in the absence of the Serbs, would you say that the Bosnian Muslim refugees also exhibited eagerness and desire to leave Srebrenica and were not forced on to the buses at that time?" When asked this by the Prosecution, the witness answered: "A. Yes, they were eager to leave, and I also think because at that time the Serb forces were not there, only the UN forces, in my mind I think also that the refugees saw the opportunity to keep their families together and board the buses and the trucks in a normal way, without pushing or kicking or brutalising in any way." Let me ask you, sir, based on your recollection, on the 13th of July at 8.00 a.m., in -- at that check-point, at that ramp, at that barricade, were there Serb forces present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes, Serb forces were present. As I understood it, this gentleman said, "I think." He said, "In my mind," which is to say that he wasn't completely certain. Perhaps there were not as many as the Serb soldiers there as there would be later. When I passed there was a group of three to four Serb soldiers who were there and who moved away for a short period of time. Women who passed afterwards said that the group of Serb soldiers later was larger. It is likely that the Serb -- that the Dutch soldier saw -- thought that the three to four Serb soldiers was a negligible group, and I disagree with his statement that the Serb soldiers were not present. They were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will ask you to tell us again, irrespective of what you said in your statement, this: The place where you saw that the men who had been separated were being kept, would you tell us how far that place was from the place where the members of international forces stood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Well, I can't be fully precise when it comes to the distance in metres but it wasn't that far. It was on the left side of the houses, and I could see well while I stood there waiting that there were a lot of people in front of me who wanted to leave. I wasn't able to leave that quickly so while I stood there I observed. I saw a vehicle TAM 80 which I knew from my army days. I saw it come in front of the house, and people, men, were separated and taken to that house. They were separated by the Serbian soldiers, which again confirms that the Serbian soldiers were already there, albeit in small numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Can you estimate the distance of that house, how far that house was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Not that far. Perhaps 20 metres. Perhaps 10 to 15 metres. Of course, one cannot be fully precise when relying on one's memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that the house was on the left side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes, on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, would you tell us looking from where was that house on the left house [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Looking from the direction in which the people were moving, from Potocari towards Srebrenica on the left side. So we were moving towards Bratunac, and it was on the left side, on the road Potocari-Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now could we see in e-court P1132, which is a book by Jean-Rene Ruez, and the collection of documents we used. Could we see page 24, please? Could we please enlarge the upper left side of this aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell me, please, looking at this photograph --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: It is too technical for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom on the middle part from the -- so that we can see the road? Could we move that to the right? Or, rather, to the left? I think that would be enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now tell us where the facility was where you were and was that the Vihor bus station or garage, rather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: It wasn't Vihor, it was Srebrenica Ekspres. That was the name of the company who had its maintenance workshop for their vehicles, and this is where I was. I was in that facility. And then the next evening I spent in destroyed buses. I can't see those buses here. Perhaps you could use my sketch. I can't really orient myself on this map. We see buses here --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, could I ask for the photograph number 25 from the same collection of photographs to be shown to the witness? Perhaps it would be better for the witness. We sort of anticipated that the witness might have problems orienting himself, so could we now see photograph 25, please? If I may also ask this middle portion to be enlarged where we can see this building with the blue roof, the road, and the building on the right-hand side. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, maybe this is a better photograph. Can you see here any buses and does this photograph remind you of the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: It is incredible how I find it so difficult to find my bearings here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if the witness is unable to find his bearings here, you should proceed, I add to this that it's totally unclear to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I suggest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. It's totally unclear to me what the issue is you are covering at this moment. It's really unclear to me. Perhaps you put questions such that the witness can answer and that clarifies what issue you are raising here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand. I will suspend this further exercise because you're obviously finding it difficult. My next question is: How did you understand the position and the role in the whole process of the evacuation of people from Potocari of members of the international forces? In your mind, what was their role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: It was completely unclear to me once I found myself in Potocari. I wasn't able to receive any protection as a person who was wounded, and it made me realise that the premonition of the people would come true, which is that all men would be executed. I noticed other men in the area who had surrendered, but these healthy men were the ones who were the most afraid. I may have some chance, being wounded, and I had the documents to prove that I was wounded at the beginning of the war on the 14th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think you've answered the question by saying that it was completely unclear to you once you found yourself in Potocari. Next question, please, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, at any point, witness members of the international forces participating in the evacuation of the population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: As I already said, I saw Dutch soldiers in front, making sure that people were passing through in smaller groups, and that after that they were checked by the Serb soldiers. That was their participation. There was no other form of participation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please now all take a look at a portion of a video, P1147? Document 28780 65 ter, V9 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Stojanovic please speak slowly the numbers? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you're invited to slowly mention the numbers. Perhaps you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so, Your Honours. P1147, Srebrenica trial video, V0009267, excerpt started from 6.00 to 6.24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is only audio at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a video clip from Potocari, following your departure, when the evacuation was nearing its completion at around half past 3.00, if we are to believe this time on the screen. This member of the Serbian army is asking his words to be translated because he was requesting members of the international forces to go over there and check whether there was anyone else who wanted to leave, and then he added that's their job. Is that how you understood the position of members of the Dutch Battalion or let's say members of the international forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think the witness has answered the question already. And I don't know that the playing of the video is in any way germane to addressing that issue further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that, it seems to be asking for opinion rather than anything else about a moment where the witness wasn't present. Mr. Stojanovic, if you have any question of fact in relation to this video, please put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before you left, were you in a position at any point to communicate with members of the international forces in any shape or form?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Only when I was exiting and when I said that there were two white APCs parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able, then, to see that those were the ones who decided the number of people to pass through in order to board the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: The Serbian forces controlled everything. That was the impression created among the people. The Serb forces even controlled them. That's what people thought and had this impression. But since I'm not an expert for this area, I would like you to ask me about what the Judge said, that you should put me the questions that I can give you answers to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for not being able to answer. We are not pressing you to do so. If you cannot answer, I shall move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have again in e-court document P1990. That's under seal and should not be broadcast. Let's look at page 4, the last paragraph in the B/C/S, and the fourth paragraph in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During examination-in-chief, you mentioned two names that you said that you later found out that they were brothers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You speak about that in the paragraph that I have just put to you. So my question is: Where were they -- according to the information that you had, where were they taken prisoner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: From what I learned during my capture, I learned that they had been captured in a different area, not in the area where the women and children were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What I'd like to ask you was whether they were captured as members of the column passing through the forest from Srebrenica towards the territory controlled by the 2nd Corps of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I don't know whether they were in the column. I know that both of them were wounded and I know that they had been brought from another location, not the location where the women and children were. That is to say not from the last check-point where I exited.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever find out what their last name was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Many people, many relatives of theirs, showed interest in order to find out what I knew, but all I can tell them was that I saw them, that they were wounded, and that they had contact with the gentleman who they addressed as a neighbour, who answered them in an angry way, and that is all the information that I could provide to their families. Now, you ask me about their last name. I did hear it, but I cannot remember it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just asking you this in order to verify the documents used by the Prosecution. Now, can you tell us whether you remembered correctly the name of the Serb soldier that they contacted, with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Stojanovic please repeat the name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Stojanovic, you said now can you tell us whether you remembered correctly the name of the Serb soldier that they contacted, with -- and then the interpreters could not hear you. Could you please repeat the name you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In the witness's statement his name is Momcilo Ristanovic, aka Zuco. I'm asking this question on account of the investigation that we are carrying out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: May I answer now? This name appeared when communicating with the relatives and friends. Savo Ristanovic is his real name. However, some people established a connection with Momcilo because they were related and probably that's why this mistake happened. His exact name is Savo Ristanovic. I just told you that the contact between these two men and him, or rather with me, was in order to find out more. When I said that they addressed the Serb soldier, they said that it could have been Momcilo but they quickly corrected themselves and said that his name was Savo Ristanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So let me try to follow what you said. Would you agree with me that the name stated in your statement, based on your subsequent knowledge, is incorrect, and that the person that you are referring to in your statement, and according to the family of these two men, was Savo Ristanovic and not Momcilo Ristanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's what the witness just explained to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I then ask one additional question? Was the nickname of Savo Ristanovic Zuco or did he have a different nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The nickname Zuco is correct. However, the family of these two lads who were killed made a wrongful connection and said Momcilo, but the real name should be Savo Ristanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now another name that you mention and I'm again asking you this for the purpose of our investigations. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We remove to private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you jumped out of the truck in which you were travelling through that hill, do you know did that truck stop at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Perhaps you misunderstood something here. If you read carefully at the statement, you will see that I had jumped out of the truck at the point where the truck was already halted, when it had already stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's see if we can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Please proceed. You're invited to make a little pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's see if we can clarify something that is not entirely clear to me. To the best of your recollection, what time of the night, and according to your testimony it was the night between the 13th and the 14th, so at what point in time that night did you jump out of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: While the Serb soldiers were still there at the school, one of them asked what time it was, and they replied to him that it was 12.00, midnight, at night. The time it took them to drive the people to the place of the execution was between 20 and 30 minutes of driving. So the time when they started the first executions was between 12.30 and 1.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look in e-court, P1999 -- 1990. And please do not broadcast that outside of the courtroom. Could we look at page 7, please, the first paragraph in the B/C/S version and page 6, the second paragraph from the bottom in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for it to appear, would it be accurate to say that you were told that you needed to go and work on repairing a shelter? Were you told that before they boarded you on those trucks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes. Some said that and the other soldier said that we were being taken to a military prison. So there were two versions: One of them said that we had to go and repair the military shelters, and the others were saying don't be afraid, you're being taken to a military prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You can read that in front of you. In your statement, this is your statement, and you said that it is consistent with your best recollections, the way it's described here is that at that time, when you were told that you needed to go to repair the shelter was at about 3.00 a.m. on 14 July 1995. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes. I see that it says that, 3.00 in early morning hours, so that is to say that we have a difference of about an hour and a half. Now, whether I was not fully precise back then, I don't know, but you can check through all of my other statements that when one Serb soldier asked the other Serb soldier what time it was, the answer was midnight. So if we take that as an accurate fact, everything else, no matter how we calculate it, cannot be fully precise. As I said to you, it took some 30 minutes to go to the execution site. So if we have this difference of about an hour and a half, I cannot fully explain it, but if you look at all of my statements, you will see that what I'm saying now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I think what Mr. Stojanovic intended to do is to draw the attention of the Chamber to a slight inconsistency of one hour or one hour and a half. You've done so, Mr. Stojanovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So let me ask you this: The shooting itself is not something that you personally observed, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: No. You again misunderstood somewhat. I said in all of my statements is that they took the people to the execution site. The truck stopped and then they started shooting people, they had already shot three men while I was still sitting on the truck. The men fell down and -- those who were being shot, and two of the people sitting on the bench with me on the truck started fleeing and were also hit by shots. So at that point in time, five people were already killed, and it is then that I jumped off the truck and started fleeing. It was night time, the terrain was steep, quite steep, which helped me in a way, and that the lights on the truck remained on, so the area in front of the truck was lit up. The side -- sides on each side of the truck were less lit, just lit up with the light that reflected off the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The people who remained on the truck outside of those five, following the moment when you jumped out, you did not see, you did not observe their execution, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes, right. I fled. I fled but I heard very loud shots that resonated, the sound resonated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How distant were you from the place where the shots were heard from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: It is very difficult to estimate the distance, especially since the terrain was quite steep and I rolled down the hill all the way down to a tiny river where I found shelter by a rock. It is from that area that I heard very loud shots resonating all the way until the end. I remained in that place until the shots stopped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Later on, you heard that that area is called Rasica Gaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You heard it from the people who are familiar with the area. My question is: Following all of these events, at any point in time, did you learn whether any exhumation had taken place there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Mr. Murat, who conducts research, he has an office in Tuzla, and at that point in time I also worked in Tuzla, so this man came to see me one day and he asked me to describe the area where the execution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was whether you heard of any exhumation at that spot. Did you or did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. I heard of the exhumation in the vicinity of that place, not at the exact location but in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That answers the question. Please, Mr. Stojanovic, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm concluding. When you say in the immediate vicinity, what exactly location are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I don't know the exact location, but if you get in touch with the gentleman I just mentioned, I know that some of the victims are already buried in the Potocari memorial centre, some of the victims who were together with me at the time of the execution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are unable to tell us what the distance was. That is the answer to the question. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, please, did you learn at any point in time where the remains of those people buried in Potocari were found, of the people mentioned by you today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I was interested before, and I'm still interested, I wanted to meet with this gentleman to learn the exact location where they were identified, and so far I haven't been able to find that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the area of Rasica Gaj, they were unable to identify any burial site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I said in the immediate vicinity, and this is what I learned from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, and if I may put another two questions, which need to be put in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, is there any need to ask further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Witness, you were asked about your recollection of the names of some of the individuals that you were with by Mr. Stojanovic on cross-examination. What I'd like to start by showing you is a document, it's 65 ter -- well, no, I'm sorry, it's P1982. It should not be broadcast, and it is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the Chamber's benefit, confidential annex D to Mr. Janc's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you were asked by Mr. Stojanovic about whether you remembered the names, full names, at least, of the individuals you were with on the date that you were nearly executed. You said you couldn't remember. And I want to ask you about this to see if it refreshes your recollection. We will need to go to page 312. And I just want to refer you to the left-hand side or column, the second from the left, and you can see a number of names there. The first one I want to direct your attention to is the individual named at number 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. (redacted) I mentioned him by name in my statement and I believe that Mr. Stojanovic asked me about him. That was a man who worked with the Dutch Battalion and who was taken to the school where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, could you please phrase your question for the witness? You've asked him to direct his attention to number 7. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My question is whether or not the information that you see relative to that individual is consistent with your recollection of his identity? That would be the age first, and obviously the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the man that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then let me ask you about similarly about the individuals listed under item number 8.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: Yes. These are the two brothers that I also mentioned, (redacted) (redacted) They were wounded and they were also brought into the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does this help refresh your recollection as to their last name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM249
utterances.text: I never mentioned their last name. It was their relatives who always mentioned their full names. Believe me that many names were mentioned and I couldn't remember all of them, so I cannot confirm this with any certainty apart from what I said that their first names were

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Let me ask you about item number 16 or rather the name that's associated with number 16. Do you recognise that name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, if you want to keep this all confidential, not to be broadcast, then reading all the names from the list is not what you're expected to do, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I haven't indicated what the document is and I think that preserves the integrity of the reason for the confidentiality, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All the references to the names will be redacted. And if you have further questions which require the names to be mentioned, please ask for private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then I'll ask for private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Witness, this concludes your testimony in this Court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. All of us who can say that we are positive human beings, we have to fight for justice and truth. I would like to say here that my aim is always to fight for justice and against hatred. In actual fact, we are talking here about the outcome of this hatred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I appreciate that you have positive feelings, but it's not the place at this moment to share them in a little speech, so you are -- it's -- would you please follow the usher? And after we have turned into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I already would like to remind the Defence that the deadline for the Rule 94 bis notice falls on the 26th of August in relation to Witness Theunens. I would have said more about it but I just remind you of that. Then I also remind the Prosecution that there are deadlines in relation to the remainder of the 92 bis and 92 quater filings. I would have said more about it if we had more time, but I just leave it at that at this very moment. And then, Mr. Registrar, we are in open session again?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the last thing I would just briefly put on the record is the following: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and the Chamber apologises to all those assisting us that we have stolen ten extra minutes from your time, and we will resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 22nd of August, 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of August, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.25 p.m.,
